Based only on the search results you provided, I'd recommend the XTAR VC4SL for most people who want a versatile 18650 battery charger. If you want the simplest budget option, the Tenergy TN270 is worth considering.

Best 18650 battery chargers
Best overall
XTAR VC4SL

Four independent bays, USB-C input, adjustable charging current up to 3A, and an LCD showing voltage, current, capacity, and internal resistance. Supports 18650, 21700, other Li-ion sizes, and NiMH/NiCd batteries.

Best for: Flashlights, hobby electronics, and people who want charging diagnostics.

Source: 1Lumen review · Best Batteries review

 Buy / check price

Nitecore UMS4

Four independent bays with QC 2.0 fast charging, up to 3A in one slot, an LCD, and compatibility with Li-ion and NiMH/NiCd cells. It also includes reverse-polarity and short-circuit protection.

Best for: Faster charging and broad battery compatibility.

Source: Official Nitecore specifications

 Buy / check price

Budget pick
Tenergy TN270

A dedicated two-bay charger with 500 mA per slot, a standard AC wall plug, reverse-polarity detection, and red/green status LEDs.

Best for: Occasional charging when speed and advanced diagnostics aren't important.

Listed price: $18.99. A 3,000 mAh cell takes approximately 6–7 hours, according to the supplied result.

XTAR VC4SL

The XTAR VC4SL has particularly useful capacity-testing and storage-mode features, according to the supplied reviews. The Nitecore UMS4 has more explicitly documented safety protections and can reach 3A in a single slot under QC mode.

Important safety note

Make sure the charger supports your battery's chemistry and voltage. Standard 18650 Li-ion cells typically use a 4.2 V charging cutoff.

Avoid charging damaged, swollen, or leaking cells.

Use a compatible power adapter and follow the manufacturer's charging instructions.

My verdict: Choose the XTAR VC4SL for the best all-around feature set. Choose the Nitecore UMS4 if charging speed and explicitly listed safety features matter more. The provided search results don't establish that either is objectively safer or more reliable than the other.
